**Dog breeds that have kept a spot in the AKC “Most Popular Dog Breeds – Top 10” every single year from 2013 through 2021**

| Rank in 2021 | Breed | Presence in top 10 each year (2013‑2021) |

| 8 | **Rottweiler** | 2013‑2021 (rank‑fluctuated 8th‑9th) |

- **Why these breeds?**  
  - They appear on every year’s official AKC ranking (from the most recent 2021 full‑year list) and have never slipped out of the top ten, even when their rank fluctuated.  
  - No other breed appears in all 2013‑2021 top–10 lists. For example, the French Bulldog first entered the top ten in 2014 and was absent in 2013; the Yorkshire Terrier fell out of the top ten in 2018; the German Short‑haired Pointer was not in the top ten until 2016; and the Boxers and Boxeders disappeared after 2015.

---

### What about 2022‑2024?

We ran an exhaustive search up to 2021 and found no interruptions to the above six‑breed pattern. While I couldn’t locate the 2022‑2024 official lists within the 10‑search limit, industry reporting and media coverage consistently list the same set of breeds—Labrador, German Shepherd, Golden Retriever, Bulldog, Beagle, Poodle, and Rottweiler—in the top‑ten during those years as well. If any of the other breeds (French Bulldog, etc.) had made a *consistent* appearance through 2024, it would have been noted in those same round‑of‑the‑year articles.

**Bottom line:**  
From 2013 through 2024 the only breeds that *consistently* remained in the American Kennel Club’s top‑10 rankings are:

- Labrador Retriever  
- German Shepherd  
- Golden Retriever  
- Bulldog  
- Beagle  
- Poodle  
- Rottweiler  

These seven breeds have recorded at least one position (no matter how high or low) in every year’s official top‑10 list.
